claim: Apple's Services segment carried a 75.6% gross margin in Q3 FY2026 versus 40.1% for Products, nearly double the Products margin.
stance_target: Services revenue deserves a materially higher multiple than Products revenue on a pure profitability basis
scope_conditions: Three months ended June 27, 2026, as reported (unaudited), consolidated (not segment-disclosed further)
quoted_support: Services 30,739 / Cost of sales Services 7,494 / Products 78,678 / Cost of sales Products 47,153 (Condensed Consolidated Statements of Operations)

claim: Services revenue growth (12.1% YoY in Q3 FY2026, 14.1% YoY nine-month) is decelerating relative to iPhone/Products growth (21.7% and 16.9% YoY respectively), reversing the pattern of prior years where Services outgrew hardware.
stance_target: Apple faces a Services growth deceleration risk that raises the required forward Services CAGR to hold total company growth flat as the iPhone 17 supercycle fades
scope_conditions: FY2026 year-to-date through Q3, vs FY2025 comparative period
quoted_support: Services 91,728 (nine months ended June 27, 2026) vs 80,408 (nine months ended June 28, 2025); Products 272,629 vs 233,287

claim: Apple's diluted share count fell from 14,948.2 million (Q3 FY2025) to 14,714.7 million (Q3 FY2026), a 1.6% YoY reduction, while EPS grew 29% YoY versus 16% revenue growth, indicating buybacks are a material EPS-growth contributor separate from operating performance.
stance_target: Buybacks raise EPS with no revenue growth, by shrinking the denominator (fundamental truth from decomposition)
scope_conditions: Q3 FY2026 vs Q3 FY2025, diluted share count and diluted EPS
quoted_support: Diluted shares 14,714,676 (thousands) vs 14,948,179; Diluted EPS 2.02 vs 1.57 (+29%)

claim: Q3 FY2026 gross margin of 50.1% included a favorable impact of approximately 2 percentage points from tariff refunds, and diluted EPS of $2.02 included a $0.11 favorable impact from the same tariff refunds — a one-time, non-recurring boost to reported margin and EPS.
stance_target: Underlying (ex-tariff-refund) Q3 FY2026 margin and EPS growth are lower than the headline figures suggest
quoted_support: Company gross margin was 50.1 percent, including a favorable impact of approximately 2 percentage points from tariff refunds. Diluted earnings per share was $2.02 ... included a favorable impact of $0.11 from tariff refunds.
region: Global (tariff-related, implies US trade policy exposure)

claim: Greater China revenue grew 22.4% YoY to $18,816M in Q3 FY2026 (nine-month Greater China revenue $64,839M, +30.0% YoY), reversing several years of China weakness for Apple.
stance_target: Persistent Greater China structural decline as a bear-case driver
scope_conditions: FY2026 quarters only; does not establish durability of the rebound
quoted_support: Greater China 18,816 / 15,369 (three months ended June 27, 2026 / June 28, 2025)
numbers: nine-month Greater China $64,839M vs $49,884M prior year (+30.0%)

claim: Products cost of sales rose faster than Products revenue is implied by the roughly stable but structurally lower Products gross margin (~40%) versus Services (~76%), meaning the durability/margin gap between the two segments persisted through FY2026 despite the iPhone 17 supercycle.
stance_target: Classifying earnings by durability (annuity-like Services vs cyclical Products) produces materially different margin profiles that justify differentiated valuation multiples
quoted_support: Total cost of sales Products 163,810 against Products net sales 272,629; Services cost of sales 21,765 against Services net sales 91,728
